ety.text: From Middle English hoby (“small horse, pony”), a variant or alteration of hobyn (“a small ambling horse”), of uncertain and disputed origin. According to one theory the term is derived from Hobin, a pet name of Robert or Robin, at the time frequently used as a proper name for a workhorse (compare dobbin).
From Middle English hoby, hobeye, from Old French hobé, hobei, hobet, from Medieval Latin hopētus, diminutive of harpe.

senses.d: An activity that one enjoys doing in one's spare time.

senses.d: An extinct breed of horse native to the British Isles, also known as the Irish Hobby.
Synonym of hobby horse (“a favorite topic”).

ety.text: Inherited from Middle French passetemps. By surface analysis, passe (“pass”) + temps (“time”).
Verb-object compound, composed of passa (“to pass”) + tempo (“time”).
Semi-learned borrowing from Latin affectiōnem (“affection”). Doublet of afección, a learned borrowing.
